title: Cash frozen in credit and stock
principle: Stock and credit are cash you can't spend. Limit both.

screens.text: September 2019: UP's sugar mills owed cane farmers ₹6,480 crore. The rule says pay in 14 days. Piyush had waited four months for ₹80,000.

screens.prompt: Piyush sold his cane. What does he really have?

options.label: A promise, and bills that won't wait

screens.why: He owed more than ₹1 lakh on a bank loan, and the bank sent him a notice. He stopped growing cane on his 30 acres.

screens.title: Frozen cash
screens.text: Money owed to you and stock freeze cash. The days from paying for stock to getting paid is your cash conversion cycle. Keep it short.

screens.title: A quick way to see it
screens.text: Each extra day of credit traps one more day of sales. Cash stuck = sales a day × days to pay. Stock works alike.

screens.prompt: Farah's printing press bills offices ₹20,000 a day. They pay after 60 days. How much of her money is with customers?
screens.why: ₹20,000 × 60 days = ₹12,00,000. That's ₹12 lakh she has earned and can't use.

screens.prompt: Farah gets new bills paid in 30 days instead of 60. How much cash comes free?
screens.why: 30 days × ₹20,000 = ₹6,00,000 still out. Before, it was ₹12,00,000. Half comes back to her.

wrong.b: Multiply sales per day by the days: ₹20,000 × 30.
wrong.c: Not all of it. Customers still take 30 days, so ₹6 lakh stays out.

screens.prompt: A bank would charge 12% a year to lend Farah that ₹6 lakh. What do faster payments save her each year?
screens.why: 12% of ₹6,00,000 = ₹72,000 a year. A shorter cash conversion cycle is the cheapest loan she'll ever get.

wrong.c: That's 12% of the full ₹12 lakh. Only ₹6 lakh comes free.

screens.prompt: Amit's phone accessory store holds ₹8 lakh of stock. He sells ₹40,000 of it a day. Keeping 8 days' stock frees how much?

wrong.a: That's what 8 days of stock costs. Take it away from the ₹8 lakh he holds now.

screens.prompt: Does it free cash or freeze it?

items.text: Ask 30% up front on big orders
Buy 3 months of stock for a bulk discount
Give a new client 90 days to pay
Keep every size in every colour
Offer 2% off for payment in 7 days

screens.why: Advances, quick payment and clearing slow stock bring cash home. Long credit and big stock piles lock it away.

screens.prompt: You're a small registered maker. A big company wants 90 days to pay. What do you ask for?

options.label: Accept 90 days. Big clients set the rules
45 days at most, written in the contract

screens.why: Since April 2024, a buyer that pays a small registered maker after 45 days can't claim that cost against tax until it pays. Use it.

wrong.a: The law is on your side. A buyer who pays after 45 days loses a tax benefit.
wrong.b: Fine if they agree, but most won't. 45 days in writing is a fair ask the law backs.

screens.setup: Imran makes steel furniture. A hotel group orders ₹10 lakh of beds, paying in 120 days. The steel and wages cost ₹7 lakh now. Imran has ₹4 lakh.
screens.question: What do you do?

options.label: Take it. Borrow the ₹3 lakh gap
options.outcome: He borrows ₹3 lakh and waits four months to be paid. A small supplier chases him, and his other orders slow down for lack of steel.
options.why: ₹7 lakh of his money sat with one client for four months.
options.better: Ask for an advance and shorter terms first.

options.label: Take it with 40% up front, rest in 45 days
options.outcome: The ₹4 lakh advance plus his ₹4 lakh covers the ₹7 lakh of costs. The other ₹6 lakh comes in 45 days, not 120.
options.why: He limited how much of his cash the client could hold, and for how long.

options.label: Turn it down. Too big for him
options.outcome: Imran stays safe but loses ₹3 lakh of profit he could have earned on better terms.
options.why: The order was fine. The terms were the problem.
options.better: Change the terms before you walk away.

summary: Money owed to you is an interest-free loan you give.
Cash stuck = sales per day × days customers take to pay.
Every day you cut from credit or stock frees cash, and saves interest.

cards.front: What do you call the days from paying for stock to getting paid by customers?
cards.back: The cash conversion cycle. Sell ₹10,000 a day with 45 days of credit, and ₹10,000 × 45 = ₹4,50,000 is stuck.

cards.back: Buyers who pay small makers after 45 days lose a tax deduction until they pay.
